column3: Free, expert SBIR/STTR proposal help can unlock major funding, but only a small minority of new founders have eligible R&D or win an award.
This is the former name of Nucleus Grow: strong SBIR/STTR help, but relevant to only a small minority of typical new founders.
Lab space, coaching, and possible funding can transform a biotech startup, but almost every typical new founder is outside its narrow, selective fit.
A regulatory waiver can be decisive, but few entry-level founders are blocked by a rule that qualifies for the sandbox.
Free, statewide one-to-one counseling is easy to reach and likely to improve a beginner's planning, pricing, financing, or next decision.
Free contracting help is valuable once government is a real customer, but that is not the typical new founder's first path.

Real credit enhancement with a published structure: Loan Participation buys down a collateralized loan, Capital Access covers borrowers without collateral. Turns a bank no into a yes. There is a lender and a decision you can go get.

Named money with named triggers: REDI grants for new high-paying rural jobs, RCOG competitive grants, Enterprise Zone credits, REDTIF post-performance reductions, Utah Rural Jobs capital access. A rural employer planning a hiring expansion should plan around it.
High-quality free education can improve an established owner, but selection and operating-history requirements exclude a typical entry-level founder.
Bilingual advising and lending are unusually useful for its audience, but the median founder may not need its specialized route.
It is mandatory and decisive for a U of U inventor, but irrelevant to nearly every typical new founder.
Microgrants and bridge loans can help SBIR/STTR applicants, but eligibility starts after a specialized federal-funding path the typical founder never enters.

Federally subsidized manufacturing extension: sales, leadership, compliance, production, and a demonstration lab, with custom engagements. Real plant-floor work at below-consultant cost, but private consultants do exist.

Free statewide site-selection support with comparative data, on-the-ground analysis, incentive navigation, and an investor network of real-estate, legal, utility, and workforce experts. Worth a morning when a Utah siting decision is actually live.
Over $1M in reported cash and services awarded across 30+ contests since 2008, plus the RAMP and LIFT accelerators and the Startup Connectory. Nondilutive prize money you can actually apply for.
The only route to federal small-business certifications — 8(a), HUBZone, WOSB — plus SBA loan-program routing and lender connections. The certifications are real assets and this is the door to them.
Export counseling from local trade specialists, foreign-partner due diligence, and federal advocacy abroad. Specific, hard to replicate privately, and free to U.S. companies.
Trade missions, market-entry programming, and support for STEP grants, which are real money against export-marketing costs. Useful only once there is something exportable.
The state pays a majority share of customized employee training, with the company contributing at least 40%. Concrete money against a real line item for an employer with staff to train.
Pathways with a guaranteed job interview on completion, TRAC classroom-plus-paid-work splits, and Utah Works short-term technical training. A structural hiring pipeline rather than a job board.
Employer tooling and incentives to stand up a registered apprenticeship, plus credentialed wage progression. Real workforce structure for a company hiring into technical roles, useless pre-revenue.

Free hybrid executive education for revenue-stage owner-operators: e-learning, live CEO masterminds, one-on-one coaching, and a three-year growth plan. Duplicates the Goldman program's shape at smaller scale.
A CDFI making microloans to founders banks reject, paired with required orientation, advising, Banking on Women, and free statewide classes. Real capital of last resort with coaching attached.
Published terms and real money: $10,000-$100,000, 6 months to 5 years, equipment/fixed assets/working capital, $75 application fee. Checkable enough to plan around.
Published RLF terms of $5,000-$250,000 for working capital and land/building purchase, with staff support through application and board review. Subordinated gap financing tied to job creation.
GetFUNDED cash awards up to $3,000, milestone-based, statewide, nondilutive, low friction. Small, but it is money and you can apply for it.
Open grant programs with named categories (grazing improvement, predatory-animal control, salinity reduction), agricultural loans, and USDA navigation. Real money for a food or livestock operator.
The Utah Outdoor Recreation Grant and related programs, plus explicit business recruitment for outdoor-recreation companies. Named grant money for a specific industry.
Runs the motion-picture incentive program — actual money against a production budget — plus location scouting, crew directories, and Film Ready community support.

Fiscal sponsorship lets an approved project accept tax-deductible donations and apply for grants requiring a nonprofit sponsor. That is a legal and financial capability that otherwise costs real money to build.
A router, but the router, and the things behind it are money: incentives, rural grants, APEX, USBCI, Opportunity Zones, with business@utah.gov as a real intake line.
Authoritative free Utah economic, demographic, and sector research. For a founder writing a market thesis or an expansion case this is the source, not a substitute for one.

Free cohort commercialization program for Utah professors, PhDs, and postdocs, ending in a pitch to active investors, at 8-10 hours a week. Specific, free, and aimed at people who genuinely cannot see the market.
The router across Nucleus Grow, UTIF, and the Nucleus Fund. Diagnosing which of three doors you need is a real service, but it is a doorway to the things that matter rather than the thing itself.
Eight weeks of free cohort training for military-connected founders through the IVMF partnership, then ongoing VBRC advising and mentorship. Structured, free, and genuinely hard to assemble alone.
One-on-one advisor sessions, the STRIVE program, an annual conference, and help getting listed as a verified veteran-owned business. The advising is the substance; the registry is not.

A single southern Utah door to SBDC counseling and APEX contracting help plus free 3D printing, a digital media studio, and laser engraving. Free tools plus free advising in one building is more than routing.

Market access and government navigation, capital access, supply-chain integration, and testbeds and demonstrations for dual-use hard tech. For a defense-adjacent Utah founder this is the practical route to Hill AFB and the primes.

$100K-$1M pre-seed with an unusually usable intake: SIV Instant promises an initial response in 24 hours, plus validation tooling and mentor access. Publishing a real front door is what separates this from the fund pages.
A long-running Mountain West seed fund actively deploying in Utah with a public portfolio to calibrate against. Worth the morning it takes to decide whether to chase a warm intro.
An established Salt Lake City early-stage software fund operating since 1986. You cannot apply your way in, but a Utah software founder raising seed should know the thesis and the stage.
A Utah seed fund with a founder-oriented team and a long local network across SaaS, commerce, fintech, and healthtech. Directory-grade for most readers, worth a morning for a matching founder.
Lehi early-stage fund since 2014 with a checkable portfolio — Podium, Degreed, Divvy, Neighbor, Owlet. Real deployment at Utah scale; still a lead, not a service.
Growth-stage capital across several named fund strategies including Traverse and the Savory Restaurant Fund, with published high-level fit thresholds. Useful once there is substantial revenue.
Salt Lake City early-stage fund since 1994 with a University of Utah Ventures partnership feeding university-linked deal flow. Established, active, and unapplyable.
Draper fund investing pre-seed through later stages with published check-size ranges by stage — more than most Utah funds disclose — plus The Stable founder community.
An established Salt Lake City early-stage technology fund, now publicly branded Run Ventures on the same domain. Note the rebrand when searching.

Medtech regulatory and quality expertise across 510(k), De Novo, PMA, IDE, EU MDR and IVDR, design controls, and QMS. For a device founder this is the difference between a submission and a wasted year, at consultant prices.
The firm that does venture financings to national standard, with a Salt Lake City office. For a venture-scale or spinout founder expecting institutional money, that reduces a real risk at real cost.

200+ attorneys covering formation, founder agreements, equity and vesting, SAFEs and priced rounds, securities compliance, and the messy contractual middle. A single established Utah firm for the whole arc.
Technology and IP transactions, licensing and joint-development agreements, IP due diligence, and patent and trade-secret strategy. Aimed squarely at founders whose value is concentrated in IP.
An IP boutique doing patent and trademark prosecution, post-issuance proceedings, portfolio management, and technology-transfer transactions. The right shape for a spinout or device team.
An IP-only Salt Lake City firm handling both prosecution and litigation. For a founder whose moat is a device, a chemistry, an algorithm, or a process, that is the specific hour worth buying.
Hands-on SBIR/STTR proposal support, training, and post-award management from a national specialist. Real expertise, but paid, and Nucleus Grow supplies much of the same free.
Lassonde Studios, Get Seeded, the Tim Draper Utah Entrepreneur Challenge, Bench to Bedside, DevLab, and Hours with Experts. Substantial for a U of U student and unavailable to anyone else.
Miller Grants, competitions, Sandbox-style venture support, and a founder peer community aimed at students holding equity by graduation. Real for BYU students, closed to everyone else.

A Provo incubator with a licensed commercial kitchen, maker space, warehouse and fulfillment staging, and staged Founders Floor milestones. The kitchen and warehouse are genuinely scarce for physical-product founders.

One Logan building holding free business counseling, an Innovation Zone makerspace with CNC and laser, a certified commercial incubator kitchen, Custom Fit training, and incubator offices. Unusual density for northern Utah.
A 50,000+ sq ft Pleasant Grove hard-tech incubator with prototyping equipment and R&D coworking for teams that have outgrown a garage. Pricing is unpublished, which caps it.
A nonprofit makerspace with tool labs for digital fabrication, woodworking, metalworking, textiles, and electronics. Affordable shared shop access is a real substitute for capital equipment.
Free statewide advising, workshops, and templates across planning, capital access, and operations for women founders. Substantive, and overlapping enough with the SBDC to cap it here.
